explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by computing Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation coefficients to quantify consistency between LLM judges and humans on GPT-4o-Audio-Preview responses

prompts.notes: Paper mentions prompts are listed in the repository but exact prompt text is not provided in the paper text

guidelines.notes: Human experts manually label whether each response is correct, following best practice for human evaluation (van der Lee et al., 2019)

sample_size.notes: Human evaluation conducted specifically on GPT-4o-Audio-Preview responses for C3 dataset

quantitative_scores.notes: All coefficients' values are more than 0.87 in either English or Chinese subset, for both LLMs

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM judges have high consistency with humans (all correlations >0.87, p<0.001) in both English and Chinese subsets, validating the reliability of the automatic evaluation method.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM judges evaluate transcribed text for most tasks, while humans also evaluate audio outputs for phonological features generation task
